Greatly improved in health since
the amputation of his left leg two
weeks
ago,
Lieutenant
Christy
Mathewson, Jr., accompanied by his
mother, will go aboard the President
Hoover tonight, preparatory to his
departure tomorrow for the United
States.
The Dollar liner is scheduled to
sail for San Francisco at 8.30 a.m.
Arriving on American soil, Lieuten-
ant Mathewson will continue cross-
continent to Washington or Balti-
more, where he will spend some
time
in Walter Read,
or Johns
Hopkins hospital, or perhaps in one
of the other large hospital centers
in the East.
After the period of hospitaliza-
tion in the
East, Lieutenant
Mathewson then will return to the
home at Saranac Lake where Mrs.
Mathewson has resided since 1921.
It was in this beautiful old home
against a wooded hillside that Mrs.
Mathewson nursed the elder Christy
Mathewson, hero of the American
baseball diamond, back to health
when he came down with tuber-
culosis after the World War. And
it is in this same home with its
deep French windows, its whito
pillars about the front, and its
gray shingle roof that Mrs. Mathew-
son hopes to nurse her son back
to health.
Lieutenant Mathewson's recupe-
ration following his operation has
been so rapid, it was learned to-
day, that he has been
up and
around in a wheel chair a great
deal in the last week and more.
He is taking his crutches along,
but as yet is unable to use them
as the left shoulder still is weak
from the injuries received in the
crash. It was on January 8 that
Lieutenant Mathewson, flying one
of the giant Sikorsky amphibians,
and with his bride of two weeks as
his only passenger, crashed against
the banks of the
Whangpoo near
Lunghwa airdrome.
Mrs.
Mathewson, Jr., suffernd
injuries in the crash from which
she died the next day, and Lieuten-
ant Mathewson himself was
SO
gravely wounded that he lay on
his back in a bed at the Country
Hospital for six months before it
was found finally necessary
to
amputate his left leg.
Despite the tragic crash, Lieuten-
ant Mathewson, according
to his
mother. continues steadfast in his
determination to return, to Hang-
chow. where he is an instructor in
the National Aviation School.
as
soon as his convalescence in
the
United States is complete. He will
not be able to fly any more, but
he hopes to continue his work in
other directions.
